I've been working this land for 40 years, same rotation my neighbors do — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same 2.6 mu used for both. My wife and I don't need to sell much, just cover our costs and keep some grain. I'm 70, so I hire the tractor for tillage and seeding. I can't do that heavy work myself anymore.

For **wheat**, I plant in mid-October after rotary tilling. I buy the improved variety from the village seed shop — same one I've used for years, yields well here. I apply compound fertilizer before planting and then urea around jointing time. I irrigate at seeding, overwintering, jointing, and heading — that's what we always do in Quzhou. I spray once for weeds in spring and once for rust or powdery mildew when it shows up. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe more if spring is good.

For **maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, it yields better. I apply base fertilizer and top-dress with urea at big bell stage. Two or three waterings is usually enough in summer — rain helps. One herbicide spray early, maybe one more if there's aphids or armyworm. Rotary till before planting. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

I keep things simple. I know what works here. I'm not trying anything new at my age.
